case_title: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Surendra Kori
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.420, 467, 468, 469, 471 r/w ss.34 and 120-B; Registration Act ss.34 and 81
evidence_type: Documentary (sale deeds, registration records), departmental and Deputy Collector enquiry reports, complainant's FIR and charge-sheet material
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged registration of more than 102 fictitious sale deeds for the same transaction to obtain Package benefits; alleged loss to the State; alleged failure to verify purchasers, sellers and land
trial_court_outcome: Not applicable; no trial verdict; charge-sheet pending
high_court_outcome: Under s.482 CrPC, FIRs, charge-sheets and criminal cases quashed (revision petitions allowed)
neutral_facts: A State Special Rehabilitation Package provided cash benefit in two instalments to persons displaced by a submerged dam project, to help them buy land. The second instalment was payable only after both seller and purchaser registered a sale deed and submitted proof of registration. Complaints alleged that various fake sale deeds were registered at the Registrar's office in Khargone to claim the benefit, and that beneficiaries were not affected by the project. A Collector's inquiry reported that some vendors were fictitious persons and that deeds were executed and registered fraudulently. Several FIRs were registered on a rehabilitation officer's complaint. The FIR for one registration recorded that a beneficiary received Rs.3,39,857 after a registration whose survey number was wrong and whose vendor could not be traced in the village. A departmental enquiry was then conducted, and it recorded procedural irregularities in registration, such as accepting photocopies of documents and not obtaining PAN details. The investigating officer alleged that the accused, a registering officer, had abetted the conspiracy and misused his position. The investigation was still continuing, and the charge-sheet stated that the accused's handwriting report and the district registrar's statement were awaited.
offence_severity: Section 81 Registration Act: up to seven years' imprisonment, or fine, or both. Minimum and punishments for IPC sections not stated in judgment
number_of_offences: 9 charged (IPC ss.34, 120-B, 420, 467, 468, 469, 471; Registration Act ss.34, 81); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Alleged loss to government of Rs.3,39,857 for one deed; alleged fraud on the Package in more than 102 deeds (prima facie)
premeditation_planning: Alleged conspiracy and planning; not decided by the Supreme Court, only prima facie indicated
motive: alleged: unlawful gain from fictitious sale deeds to obtain Special Rehabilitation Package benefits
key_evidence_accepted: None finally accepted; Court relied only on prima facie material in FIRs, charge-sheets and enquiry reports
post_offence_conduct: Suspended from service by Registration Department after enquiry
custody_duration: Not stated (charge-sheet says accused was arrested; duration not given)
trial_duration: offence: 1.4.2005 to 31.3.2007 (registrations); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 22.01.2009; Supreme Court: 26.09.2012
legal_representation: Accused (respondent): Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad. State (appellant): Sidharth Dave, Abhimanyu Singh, C.D. Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered 18.9.2007; charge-sheet No. 546 of 2007 filed under s.173(8); investigation continuing
procedural_irregularity: Enquiry found photocopies accepted, fees not realised, s.64 memos not sent, affidavits and PAN details missing, photocopies of certificates accepted
appeal_history: Trial court: no trial (charge-sheet pending). High Court: FIRs and charge-sheets quashed under s.482 CrPC. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, High Court judgments set aside
prosecution_argument: Registrar is liable if prima facie instrumental in aiding fictitious sale deeds to obtain Package benefits; large number of deeds could not be executed without his knowledge or connivance
defence_argument: Registrar was bound only to register documents under the Registration Act and had no duty to verify genuineness or title; no knowledge of forgery
legal_principle_applied: Inherent power under s.482 CrPC to be used sparingly; High Court should not give prima facie decision on hazy facts or evaluate evidence; knowledge questions require evidence at trial
precedent_relied_upon: M.M.T.C. Ltd v. Medchl Chemicals & Pharma (2002) 1 SCC 234; State of Orissa v. Saroj Kumar Sahoo (2005) 13 SCC 540; Eicher Tractors Ltd v. Harihar Singh (2006) 12 SCC 763; Jambu Prasad v. Mohammad Nawab Aftab Ali Khan AIR 1941 PC 16 (referred)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Magnitude of alleged crime and number of allegedly fraudulent documents, which required trial evidence
other_sentence_order: None; Court's observations are prima facie and do not bind the trial court
